questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: What symptom duration is required for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis in the source?
questions.exp: Diagnosis of RA is based on duration of symptoms greater than 6 weeks. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which duration label is printed for 0–3 months of symptoms?
questions.exp: 0–3 months is labelled very early rheumatoid arthritis. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which duration label is printed for more than 2 years?
opts: Chronic stabilized rheumatoid arthritis with deformities
questions.exp: More than 2 years is labelled chronic stabilized rheumatoid arthritis with deformities. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which feature statement best matches RA at the chapter start?
opts: Most common multisystem autoimmune inflammatory connective tissue disease with arthritis/arthralgia and chronic inflammatory symmetrical peripheral polyarthritis
questions.exp: RA is described as the most common multisystem autoimmune inflammatory CTD with arthritis/arthralgia and chronic inflammatory symmetrical peripheral polyarthritis. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which upper-limb joints are involved in RA and which are spared according to the table?
opts: PIP, MCP and rare elbow involved; DIP and 1st CMC spared
DIP and 1st CMC involved; MCP spared
questions.exp: Upper-limb RA involves PIP, MCP and rarely elbow; spared joints include DIP due to least synovium and 1st CMC. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which lower-limb and axial pattern is printed for RA?
opts: 1st MTP involved with 5th MTP spared; lumbar spine involved
Sacroiliac joint as the main involved site
Hip and shoulder root joints only
5th MTP and rare knee involved; 1st MTP spared; C1-C2 spine involved with thoracic/lumbar/sacral vertebrae spared
questions.exp: RA lower limb involves 5th MTP and rarely knee, spares 1st MTP; axial skeleton involves C1-C2 and spares thoracic, lumbar and sacral vertebrae. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which extra-articular statement is printed at the end of the joint table?
opts: 40% of RA patients have extra-articular manifestations, most commonly rheumatoid nodules
Extra-articular disease never occurs in RA
All patients have rheumatoid lung first
Uveitis is the most common manifestation
questions.exp: The page states 40% of RA patients have extra-articular manifestations, with rheumatoid nodule most common. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: DIP involvement suggests which diseases in the RA note?
opts: Psoriatic arthritis, osteoarthritis, multicentric reticulohistiocytosis and CPPD disease
questions.exp: The DIP note lists psoriatic arthritis, osteoarthritis as the most common arthritis, multicentric reticulohistiocytosis and calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate disease. (Book p521)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which pathogenesis sequence is printed for RA initiation?
opts: ANCA activates neutrophils after LPS only
Genetics plus environment causes abnormal protein modification such as citrullination/carbamylation, antigen detection by Langerhans dendritic cells and T-cell interaction
Cryoglobulins precipitate in cold then dissolve on warming
questions.exp: The RA pathogenesis diagram starts with genetics plus environment, abnormal protein modification such as citrullination/carbamylation, detection as antigen by Langerhans dendritic cells and DC-T interaction. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which cytokine is labelled the key pathogenic cytokine in RA?
questions.exp: The diagram labels TNF-alpha as the key pathogenic cytokine. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: How does pannus-related joint damage appear in the RA diagram?
opts: Chronic synovitis with synovial hypertrophy forming pannus and periarticular erosion/osteopenia
questions.exp: The normal joint progresses to chronic synovitis with synovial hypertrophy, pannus and periarticular erosion/osteopenia. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which pathway from TNF-alpha to osteoporosis is printed?
opts: TNF-alpha activates osteoclast through RANK ligand pathway and inhibits osteoblast through Dkk-1
TNF-alpha blocks osteoclast and increases osteoblast
questions.exp: TNF-alpha activates osteoclast via RANK ligand pathway and inhibits osteoblast via Dkk-1, leading to osteoporosis. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which HLA factor is printed as major RA risk with shared epitope?
opts: DRB1-04, 70%, fivefold risk, shared epitope QKRAA motif
questions.exp: HLA DRB1-04 is listed in 70%, increases risk five times and has shared epitope QKRAA motif. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which HLA factor is associated with protection in RA?
questions.exp: The genetic HLA list notes DR-13 is associated with protection. (Book p522)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which non-HLA factor is seen in Asian populations and what does it do?
opts: PADI-4 converts arginine to citrulline by post-translational modification
PTPN22 converts citrulline to arginine and is seen in Asians
questions.exp: PADI-4 is peptidyl arginine deiminase IV, post-translationally modifying arginine to citrulline and is seen in Asian populations. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which non-HLA factor is not seen in Asian population according to the source?
questions.exp: PTPN22 is specifically noted as not seen in the Asian population. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which environmental factor is the strongest harmful RA risk factor and what does it increase?
opts: Smoking, increasing PADI-4 expression in airway and ILD risk
questions.exp: Smoking is the strongest environmental risk factor, increases PADI-4 expression in airway and increases risk for ILD with bad prognosis. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which environmental factors are protective in RA?
questions.exp: Protective environmental factors listed are alcohol and OCP. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: Which gender and infection statements are printed?
opts: Females exceed males 3:1; male presentations more often include ILD and vasculitis; Porphyromonas gingivalis chronic periodontitis is linked
Males exceed females 9:1 with no infection link
Children are most affected and infection is HCV
Sex distribution is equal and periodontal disease is protective
questions.exp: Other factors list females > males 3:1, most common presentation in males as ILD/vasculitis, and infection Porphyromonas gingivalis chronic periodontitis. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: What pregnancy effect is printed in RA?
questions.exp: Pregnancy is listed as increased IL-10 inducing remission. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: In the acute inflammatory polyarthritis risk-prediction flow, what happens at 6 weeks?
opts: Persistent disease becomes undifferentiated arthritis; reduced disease becomes post-viral
questions.exp: The risk-prediction flow shows acute inflammatory polyarthritis at 6 weeks: persistent goes to undifferentiated arthritis and reduced goes to post-viral. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
questions.q: What are the three equal outcomes of persistent undifferentiated arthritis in the printed flow?
opts: Half evolve to RA and half to OA
Two-thirds become gout and one-third MPA
One-third remission, one-third persistent/progress to other disease, one-third evolve to RA
questions.exp: Undifferentiated arthritis branches into one-third remission, one-third persistent/progress to other disease and one-third evolve to RA. (Book p523)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which variables are included in the printed score for predicted risk of RA?
opts: Age, female sex, joint distribution, swollen joints, tender joints, CRP, rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibody
questions.exp: The predicted-risk score lists age, female, joint distribution, swollen joints, tender joints, CRP, rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibody. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: What does a predicted-risk score above 8 imply in the source?
opts: More than 80% chance to progress to RA
questions.exp: The page states if score >8 there is >80% chance to progress to RA. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which anti-CCP/ACPA statement is printed?
opts: Used for diagnosis and not repeated; specificity >90%; best marker for preclinical infection; high titre suggests extra-articular manifestations
Specificity 75–80% and non-specific in 5% of normal population
questions.exp: Anti-CCP/ACPA/MCV is used for diagnostic purpose and not repeated, specificity >90%, best marker for preclinical infection and high titre suggests extra-articular manifestations. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which rheumatoid factor statement is printed?
opts: Specificity >99% and never occurs outside RA
IgA RF is most common and against IgG Fc
Used only for relapse, not diagnosis
Specificity 75–80%, marker of preclinical infection, suggests extra-articular manifestations and is nonspecific in several diseases and 5% normal population
questions.exp: RF specificity is 75–80%, it is a marker of preclinical infection and extra-articular manifestations, and is nonspecific in cryoglobulinemia, Sjogren, JIA, 5% normal population, infections and other diseases. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which antibody detail is printed for rheumatoid factor?
opts: IgM is most common against IgG Fc; IgA RF occurs in Caplan syndrome
IgG is most common against IgA Fc; IgM occurs only in SLE
IgE is most common against IgM Fc
RF is an anti-citrullinated peptide only
questions.exp: RF antibodies are shown as IgM most common against IgG Fc, with IgA in Caplan syndrome. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which markers are printed for relapse?
questions.exp: For relapse, the page lists CRP and ESR. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which articular presentation is printed as most common in RA?
opts: Axial spine pain relieved by rest
Chronic inflammatory symmetric peripheral polyarthritis, insidious in 55–65%
questions.exp: The clinical manifestation section begins with chronic inflammatory symmetric peripheral polyarthritis and notes insidious presentation in 55–65% as most common. (Book p524)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: An elderly patient over 60 has acute destructive painful erosive polyarthritis mimicking PMR with shoulder/pelvic pain, raised ESR and periarticular enthesitis/bursitis. Which RA variant is printed?
questions.exp: Elderly RA is >60 years, acute destructive polyarthritis with painful erosions and mimics PMR with shoulder/pelvic pain, increased ESR and periarticular enthesitis/bursitis. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A patient has minimal symptoms but erosions on X-ray. Which printed RA variant is this?
questions.exp: Arthritis robustus is described as minimal symptoms, blissfully unaware, with erosions on X-ray. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Young girls have recurrent acute episodic monoarthritis with complete resolution, later involving other joints, anti-CarP positivity and 30% progression to RA. What is this?
questions.exp: Palindromic rheumatism occurs in young girls, acute episodic monoarthritis with complete resolution and later other joints, anti-CARP positive, with 30% progressing to RA. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: The source's synovitis deformity triangle contains which three processes?
questions.exp: The deformities triangle is labelled synovitis, tendinitis and bursitis. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A hand shows wrist radial deviation, MCP ulnar deviation plus subluxation, and interphalangeal joints extended. Which reversible deformity is printed?
questions.exp: Zig-zag deformity is the first change and includes wrist radial deviation, MCP ulnar deviation plus subluxation and interphalangeal joints extended. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A patient has rupture of the ulnar collateral ligament and deformity of the ulnar styloid. Which reversible deformity is this?
questions.exp: Piano-key deformity is due to rupture of the ulnar collateral ligament and deformity of the ulnar styloid. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A thumb has a Z-shaped deformity with abduction and hyperextension. Which RA deformity is printed?
questions.exp: Hitchhiker thumb is a Z-shaped deformity with abduction and hyperextension of the thumb. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Trigger finger in RA is attributed to what?
questions.exp: Trigger finger is listed as tenosynovitis. (Book p525)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A hand has hyperextended PIP, flexed DIP and rupture of the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon. Which irreversible deformity is this?

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: A hand has PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension from PIP synovitis with lateral band subluxation. Which deformity is this?
questions.exp: Boutonniere deformity is flexion of PIP and hyperextension of DIP due to synovitis of PIP causing subluxation of the lateral band. (Book p526)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities

questions.exp: Opera glass hand deformity is labelled arthritis mutilans. (Book p526)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
questions.q: Which features define intrinsic plus deformity?
opts: Radial wrist deviation with MCP ulnar deviation
Tight intrinsic muscles with hyperflexion of MCP and extension of interphalangeal joints
questions.exp: Intrinsic plus deformity is tightness of intrinsic muscles, hyperflexion of MCP and extension of interphalangeal joints. (Book p526)

questions.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities

questions.exp: The note states pointing index finger is median nerve palsy. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Extra-articular RA and RA versus SLE

questions.sec: Extra-articular RA and RA versus SLE
questions.q: Which ocular statement belongs to RA?

questions.sec: Extra-articular RA and RA versus SLE

questions.q: If response is adequate after methotrexate, what does the algorithm direct?

questions.sec: RA management
questions.q: For inadequate response using methotrexate plus sulfasalazine, what dose and maximum are printed?

questions.sec: RA management

questions.sec: RA management

opts: Less costly, most preferred, cardiac toxicity and hyperlipidemia

units.title: 1. RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
units.sec: RA diagnosis duration, joint involvement and etiopathogenesis
units.guide:
Duration-based labels, chronic symmetric peripheral polyarthritis and spared/involved joints open RA.
Pathogenesis diagram, pannus, TNF-alpha, Dkk-1 and osteoporosis are retained.
Genetic, environmental, gender, age, pregnancy, infection and risk-prediction points follow in order.

units.title: 2. RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
units.sec: RA prediction markers, clinical manifestations and deformities
units.guide:
Predicted-risk scoring factors and serologic markers lead into chronic symmetric peripheral polyarthritis.
RA variants, palindromic rheumatism and deformity mechanisms are retained.
Reversible and irreversible hand deformities and median nerve note are kept in source order.

units.title: 3. Extra-articular RA and RA versus SLE
units.sec: Extra-articular RA and RA versus SLE
units.guide:
The extra-articular comparison table is captured by pulmonary, CNS/PNS, ocular, vascular, hematologic, cardiac, GIT, endocrine and skin rows.
RA and SLE contrasts are retained as book-study material.
High-yield complication triggers such as atlantoaxial subluxation, vasculitis, Felty and lung disease are explicitly asked.

units.title: 4. RA management
units.guide:
Newly diagnosed RA targets remission/low activity, with very early RA best response under 3 months.
Conventional DMARD mechanisms, biologics and JAK inhibitors are retained.
The treatment algorithm includes bridge steroid therapy, methotrexate dosing, toxicities, Boolean remission and escalation choices.
